text1: Rendelli StarDrive's Model 805R is about as plain as a starship gets, and about as useful. Cheap and compact, it is the ship of choice for small shipping firms and charter outfits, and it doubles as a courier. Under the boxy shell is a tough little frame that keeps flying long after flashier ships are scrapped; there is one in nearly every port.

Metroworks' V7 is little more than three big engines joined to a cargo hold and a life-support module, and that is the whole idea: nothing gets a load there faster or from farther away. Starbound Express trusts it with almost all of its domestic routes.

Allied Shipyards' AS129 has been a best-seller for a decade. It is neither quick nor nimble and does not hold up well under fire, but nothing in its class hauls more; the CDX Argosy, its nearest rival, comes up short on capacity.

Aerostar Space Industries mostly makes subassemblies for other shipyards, but its C-35 Star Clipper Mk. IV is the product everyone recognises. The sleek delta-winged hull is half courier and half light warship, outfights most ships its size, and has room to be built up into a quick hauler or a heavy fighter.

CDX Starworks sells the I-287B Defender mostly to corporations and small governments guarding their own space. Nothing in production is faster or more agile, but its thin protection keeps it an in-system interceptor rather than a strike craft, and even the Mk. II's larger tanks only stretch its range so far.

The F/A-927E Rapier is CDX Starworks' best seller and carries more firepower than anything else in its class. All that weight makes it the clumsiest of its peers, yet bounty hunters, corporate governments and anyone wanting a harder punch keep buying it.

Maskirovka's IPV-1 Corvette resists easy labels: it accelerates and turns like a heavy fighter but carries the armament of a light capital ship. Built to fill the gap between starfighters and the Atinoda Kestrel, it is a favourite customs and patrol ship of corporate governments.

CDX Starworks built fighters before it built freighters, and the Argosy shows it. Quicker, nimbler and better armed than the AS129, it has won over shippers working the edge of Confederation space; the price is a higher sticker and a little less room in the hold.

The Atinoda Kestrel is the most powerful ship sold to civilians, and Atinoda only sells it to its most reputable buyers. Besides its own weapon mounts it carries two launch bays, which is why it counts as an escort ship. Rumour has it that a freighter full of Kestrel parts vanished near the edge of Confederation space...

The AS1300 from Allied Shipyards is the only true bulk freighter on the market. Too expensive and too lightly defended to risk on the frontier, it rules the inner lanes instead, where these giants move most of the trade between the Core Worlds.

Terran Naval Yards' G-564 missile gunboat is a stretched relative of the P-361 patrol fighter and shares much of its hardware, including the distinctive three-part wing assemblies. The forward strakes along its fuselage are built to carry missiles and rockets.

Terran Naval Yards builds the FF-4237 for the Confederation Navy alone. It is rugged and adaptable, and Navy bulletins boast that it outclasses the Kestrel and any escort the Rebellion can field, and that task forces built around it will crush the rebels. The Navy still calls it a frigate, though it is a cruiser by any other measure.

The CR-1095 heavy cruiser grew out of Terran Naval Yards' FF-4237 frigate and looks much like it, only far larger. The Confederation is counting on these ships, each carrying its own patrol craft, to bring the Rebellion to its knees.

The Rebel destroyer began as a pitch from engineers who defected from CDX Starworks. It is in essence an Argosy with stronger engines and more guns, which makes it cheap to build in numbers. Still a freighter at heart, it cannot match the Confederate frigate or the Kestrel, but it is a mainstay of the Rebel fleet.

A bulk freighter gutted by Rebel shipwrights and refitted with four launch bays, plus two more improvised in its old cargo hold. It carries no guns at all and its systems are bare-bones, so it fields swarms of cheap Manta interceptors and dies quickly if they ever leave it alone. Rarely seen unless the Confederation is hunting the Rebel fleet in force.

Working in secret from crude bases on backwater worlds, Rebel shipwrights produced one of the finest and deadliest warships in space. Its ring-shaped engine pylons double as docking racks for Manta fighters, so the whole squadron can launch almost at once.

Terran Naval Yards' P-361 patrol fighter, which the Navy calls the finest starfighter ever built; certainly no one has publicly reported one losing a dogfight. In this sector it flies from Confederate cruisers as a shielded heavy fighter.

Astrotech's F-37B Manta flew for the Confederation early in the Great War before its light armament put it out of fashion. When Astrotech went bankrupt, its leftover stock was quietly bought by an unknown party, and now freighter crews report attacks by small triangular fighters. The Rebellion's fast, agile interceptor.

A light fighter designed only to operate from the launch bays of larger ships. Not fast or agile, but sturdy and cheap: any large hull can carry a bay of them, and they hold the line where Mantas would scatter. Each carries decoy flares that draw point-defence fire away from its wingmates.

Blazitron Industries' F-563 Lightning fighter-bomber pairs speed and agility with heavy firepower, a design clever enough to win industry awards. This is the F-563N, the version adapted for shipboard launch; a single Lightning flies from each of a Kestrel's bays.

The standard civilian starship weapon: a compact coherent-light cannon that throws a rapid stream of green bolts. Sold both as a swivel turret and as a forward-firing cannon; the fixed version's longer focusing barrel gives it extra reach.

A particle accelerator that fires dense packets of protons - the workhorse weapon of both navies. Fitted to a turret ring it covers every angle; mounted as a fixed forward cannon, the full-length accelerator gives it considerably more range.

Fleet-grade heavy cannon that hurls a superheated neutron charge. Each shot hits like a torpedo, but the mounting is slow to traverse and the blaster draws enormous power. Built only for capital ships.
A lightweight Laser Cannon built into the frame of a fighter.
A Manta's single Laser Cannon, slaved to a fast-tracking fire computer that picks off incoming missiles and enemy fighters first.
A lightweight Proton Cannon built into the frame of a Confederate patrol craft.

A Rebel favourite: an electromagnetic rail that hurls dense metal slugs. The slugs are slow enough to dodge at long range, but each one slams into shields hard, and the rails reach further than any laser.
Two heavy rockets carried by a fighter. Reloaded at the carrier.
Two guided concussion missiles carried by a fighter. Reloaded at the carrier.
A small rack of self-guided concussion missiles. Fire-and-forget, with enough punch to finish a fighter or crack a damaged hull.
Heavy unguided rockets, fired one at a time. Fast and armoured enough to slip past light point defence, and each one hits hard enough to crack plating.
Heavy homing torpedoes with a capital-ship warhead. They crawl toward their target, but their armoured casings shrug off point defence and their guidance rarely lets go.

After the Great War against the alien invaders, the core worlds' wartime union refused to give up its power. The Confederation now rules the core worlds with the backing of its powerful Navy, based at Ruby in the Antares system, and is locked in a bloody stalemate with the Rebellion of the outer colonies.

The outer colonies, stripped of resources and denied a voice in the Senate, rose against the Confederation. With help from sympathetic corporations the insurrection has grown into a formidable navy based at Palshife.
Ruby is completely red: red ground, red sky, red planet in the background. This moon is a testing ground for many new Confederation weapons.
Luna is New Providence's only moon, and home to the main shipyards of the Terran Naval Yards. Its weak gravity and almost perfect vacuum make it an ideal place to build heavy warships.
P-6564 is a planet shrouded by a corrosive atmosphere. Better not stay too long, or your ship might melt.

New Providence is a peaceful world, founded long ago during the Great Expansion. During the Great War, the Confederation converted the once-agrarian colony into a huge mining operation, run by the Confederation-loyal Astex Mining Corporation.

Due to the postwar rise in commercial traffic in the vicinity of the Antares system, the Confederation has constructed this small orbital garrison. It serves as a refuelling base for Confederation patrol ships, as well as a vanguard against possible Rebel incursions against the mines of New Providence.

Palshife is a beautiful world of rocky islands and gorgeous skies. It was one of the galaxy's more popular vacation spots, before the Great War. Now, it is home to the Rebel High Command and the Rebellion's main troop-training center and shipyard.
Clotho Prime is often visited by Rebel warships, as the Rebellion maintains a repair and refuelling base on the surface of the planet.
Rupert is a small moon that is home to a colony of religious fanatics, followers of the Order of the Holy Mac.

Turin V is an arid, barren world, characterized by freezing temperatures and fierce winds. The colony ship Sojourner II was the first ship to reach this planet, and was forced to crash-land in the desert when its propulsion and life support systems were destroyed by a meteorite.

Spica is a world shrouded by toxic clouds and a choking atmosphere. The uridium miners who work here have the highest fatality rate of any in the galaxy, as even a brief accidental exposure to Spica's atmosphere is instantly fatal.
Levo is an independent world that has resisted joining the Confederation. Anyone is welcome at the tiny but neutral Levo Spaceport, located on the island of Locanda in Levo's southern ocean.

Blackthorne is an extremely dangerous place for a law-abiding citizen to hang out. If you don't actually get your cargo stolen, you'll at least get your pocket picked. Still, Blackthorne is the place to come if you're looking for any of the "special" items available here.
